results.content: # Market shrugs off in-line July CPI report. NEW YORK, Aug 12 (Reuters) - U.S. consumer prices increased slightly in July, potentially weakening the argument for an interest rate increase from the Federal Reserve next month. The Consumer Price Index edged up 0.1% last month after dropping 0.4% in June, which was the first decline in six years, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Wednesday. In the 12 months through July, the CPI advanced 3.4% after rising 3.5% in June.
